purpose: Fix the common stretch factor k of work 2 (decisions 3 and 4 of .steering/20261028-while-waiting-2) from the window means of 40 reference works of other authors in Aozora Bunko, before the works of work 2 are chosen. The reference works are not candidates of work 2: the six candidate authors are excluded in every role, and so is any work in which one of them takes part.
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-10-27 and committed, with the script and the code it runs, before the script was run. No reference work had been fetched or read; no value of any Japanese text other than the self-written check sentences (checks/conditions/japanese_map_sensitivity.json) and the test sentences of tests/ had been computed. The rule for k (0.9 over the weighted 0.99 quantile of max(|V|, |A|)) and the number of works (40) were decided by the researcher before this file was written. k is written into the conditions of work 2 after this run, before the choice of the second author arrives. Revised before any run after independent reviews (Codex and a code review by Claude): network failures stop the run instead of skipping a work, the settings of the window, the step and the rule for k are compared with the code, the exclusion is checked again on the rows of the list, the versions of fugashi and ipadic are compared, and the leave-one-out readout was added.

eligible.row: 文字遣い種別 = 新字新仮名, 作品著作権フラグ = なし, 役割フラグ = 著者, 分類番号 (stripped) = NDC 913, テキストファイル符号化方式 = ShiftJIS, テキストファイルURL ends with .zip
eligible.work: exactly one row with 役割フラグ = 著者 for the 作品ID, and none of the excluded persons in any row of the 作品ID
eligible.sentences_rule: the number of sentences after strip_aozora -> strip_date_note -> split_sentences (src/pipeline.work2_body), the same as for the candidates
eligible.not_filtered: literary (文語) works cannot be told from the list and are not excluded; works in the old orthography are excluded by 文字遣い種別

draw.rule: rng = numpy.random.default_rng(seed). The persons with at least one eligible work, sorted by 人物ID, are put in the order rng.permutation(number of persons). For each person in that order, the person's eligible works sorted by 作品ID are put in the order rng.permutation(number of works) (drawn when the person is reached); the works are fetched in that order and the first whose text gives a number of sentences in the range is taken (one work per person; a work that fails to fetch, unzip, decode as cp932 or pass strip_aozora is skipped and recorded with its reason). The draw stops when n_works are taken; it is an error if the persons run out first.
draw.fetch: urllib, a pause of 1 s between requests, timeout 60 s. A failed request, an HTTP error or a body that is not a zip stops the run (it must not change the draw); a rerun continues with the zips kept so far. Only the content of a fetched zip can skip a work (not one .txt member, not cp932, or rejected by strip_aozora). The zips are kept in external/reference-stretch-20261028/zips/<人物ID>/ (written to a temporary name, then renamed) with their SHA-256.

step.steps: src/japanese_text.strip_aozora (header to the second line of hyphens, footer from 底本： or ［＃本文終わり］, ruby, headings, notes), src/japanese_text.strip_date_note (decision 2 of .steering/20261028-while-waiting), src/japanese_text.split_sentences, src/japanese_text.sentence_point, src/window.trajectory, src/stretch.stretch

map.use: map B: V = 0.40982 x - 2.01110, A = 0.42190 x - 1.69426 per word, clipped to [-1, 1], then averaged

window.rule: decision 4 of .steering/20261028-while-waiting: one sentence at a time, every window of W sentences (no padding), position (start + W/2) / n, matched sentences with equal weight, a gap if fewer than half are matched, works never joined

k_rule.of: max(|V|, |A|) of every window with a point (gaps left out) of the unstretched trajectories
k_rule.weights: each work the same total weight, shared equally by its windows with a point
k_rule.quantile_method: values sorted ascending, weights normalised to sum 1; the smallest value whose cumulative weight reaches the quantile (within 1e-12)

readouts: the weighted share of reference windows clipped under k (stretch.clip_rate)
k with each reference work left out in turn: the smallest and the largest, and which work they leave out (a sensitivity fixed before the run, as Codex advised; it does not change k)

per reference work: person, work ID, title, URL, zip SHA-256, txt name, body SHA-256, sentences, shares of matched sentences and tokens, windows and gaps, and the 1, 50 and 99 percentiles (nearest index) of V, of A and of max(|V|, |A|) over its windows
the same percentiles pooled over the works with the weights of k_rule, for V and A before and after the stretch
the works skipped in the draw and why
not_claimed: That k fits the works that will be chosen: the reference works are other authors, of other periods and kinds, and a stretch fixed on them is not guaranteed to suit any chosen author. The differences of lexicon coverage between authors are made larger by the stretch too. Both are written with the work.
